_pricing_note: pricing.{prompt_per_m,completion_per_m} (USD per million tokens) is a 2026-08-27 snapshot from public list prices, used by leaderboard.sh (#92) to ESTIMATE cost_usd on rows the provider does not bill for (tokens_prompt/tokens_completion present, no cost_usd). Values pulled from the corresponding seat's `notes` field where a price was already documented there; null where no price was known with reasonable confidence (deepseek, mimo, minimax, kimi27, kimi3 — no confirmed current list price on hand) or where the seat is a CLI lane with no token counts at all (codex, antigravity, gemini-pro, kimi). Refreshing these against the live OpenRouter catalog belongs to validate_or_models.sh, not this field.
_doc: Per-reviewer behavioral profile. Read by run_reviewers.sh (timeout, retry, model), the SKILL.md synthesis step (severity_priors, synthesis_weight), and analyze_runlog.sh (suggests edits to this file). Tune values here, not in scattered defaults. Edit notes/specialization freely; numeric tuning is best driven by analyze_runlog.sh suggestions over real runs. NOTE: antigravity and gemini-pro are BOTH served by Google's `agy` (Antigravity) CLI as of the 2026-06-18 Gemini-CLI sunset — the only difference is the --model value. The `model` field here MUST be the exact display-name string `agy models` prints (e.g. "Gemini 3.1 Pro (High)"); agy silently falls back to its default (Flash) on an unrecognized model string instead of erroring.

codex.specialization: general — agentic file roaming with built-in review prompt; roams before it reports, so duration scales with repo surface, not diff size
codex.notes: Reliable in observed runs (4/4 most rounds). Treat solo P1 as near-certain real. Output sometimes truncates on very long sessions — surface the truncation in the runlog rather than retrying. timeout_s 300 → 900 on 2026-08-14, per Gabriel: the 300s budget was set on a 'fast-or-fail' read that no longer holds. On a 268-line, 18-file diff codex burned the full 300s producing 224KB of context-gathering log and no review at all — it is agentic, so it explores the repo before writing anything, and the budget cut it off mid-exploration. A timeout that lands before the reviewer has said one word is not a tuning signal, it is a lost baseline seat.

antigravity.specialization: architecture, side-effects, cross-file reasoning; agentic file-reading via Google's `agy` CLI on Gemini 3.7 Flash. Fast lap of the Gemini fleet. Rotation-pool member (not a baseline).
antigravity.notes: Replaces the prior `gemini` (Gemini CLI Flash) reviewer slot, retired in the 2026-06-18 Gemini-CLI consumer sunset. Binary: `agy` (install: `curl -fsSL https://antigravity.google/cli/install.sh | bash`, lands in ~/.local/bin; auth: `agy login` once). Model is pinned via `--model "Gemini 3.7 Flash (High)"` — must match an `agy models` display name exactly or agy silently uses its default. Solo findings have lower precision than convergent ones — weight accordingly. EMPTY OUTPUT: check meta.json failure_kind + the .agy.log tail before diagnosing — quota_exhausted (shared 'Individual quota', 429, resets on a ~2-day cadence; observed 2026-07-01: agy exits 0 with empty stdout in ~5s) is at least as common as expired `agy login` auth. FALLBACK POLICY REVISED 2026-08-22 (supersedes the 2026-07-01 no-fallback rule): on an ACCOUNT wall (quota/auth/suspension) or an agy panic this lap is re-run over OpenRouter against the same Gemini model, loudly — see or_fallback above. It is recorded as status "fallback", never "ok", so the leaderboard still down-weights the sick lane. On any other failure the lap still drops out and rotation covers the gap. MODEL BUMPED 2026-08-22: Gemini 3.5 Flash (High) → 3.7 Flash (High). agy had been listing 3.6 and 3.7 Flash for weeks while this seat stayed pinned to 3.5 — detection never noticed because detect_reviewers.sh only greps the models list for a 3.1 Pro entry, and the 6h agy_models.txt cache hid the rest. No draw_boost: a Flash point-release is the same seat, not a new identity (contrast deepseek/nemotron in #59, which changed tier and model outright).

gemini-pro.specialization: deep reasoning, multi-step logic, architectural and semantic-drift findings the Flash lap misses. Slower and more expensive than antigravity (Flash). Deep lap of the Gemini fleet. Rotation-pool member (not a baseline).
gemini-pro.notes: DRAW_BOOST 2.5 SET 2026-08-27: best precision in the fleet outside the codex baseline — 152 findings over 157 seats at a 10% fact-check drop rate, free, and ~3x antigravity's per-seat yield (1.1 vs 0.4 findings/run). It was being drawn far below what that record earns. Deliberately a heavy boost and NOT a third baseline: baselines sit on the fail-closed path in select_roster.sh and this is a preview-tier model, so it must be allowed to vanish without blocking a round. Shared-Google-quota risk checked and is not real in the data: 1 quota_exhausted event across 592 combined agy seats (gemini-pro + antigravity), plus the OpenRouter fallback added 2026-08-22. Same `agy` CLI as antigravity, just pinned to `--model "Gemini 3.1 Pro (High)"`. Previously routed through the standalone `gemini` CLI (-m gemini-3.1-pro-preview); migrated to agy in the 2026-06-18 sunset since agy now hosts Gemini 3.1 Pro and exposes --model. Pro is a preview tier — surface model-availability errors to the user, don't auto-retry. NOTE: antigravity + gemini-pro are the SAME provider (Google) — their agreement is NOT independent the way codex/kimi convergence is; treat Flash+Pro overlap as one provider's vote, not two. Pro triggers agy's SIGSEGV panic (RunCommandHandler nil-deref, agy ≤1.0.15) far more than Flash — it roams files/commands harder; exit 2 + ~20-45s + empty output = the panic, not your diff. Quota semantics: same as antigravity (check failure_kind). FALLBACK POLICY REVISED 2026-08-22: an ACCOUNT wall or an agy panic re-runs this lap over OpenRouter against the same Pro model (see or_fallback); any other failure still drops the lap. Recorded as status "fallback", never "ok".

kimi.specialization: single-turn correctness, race conditions, defensive guards; reasons on the diff as given without tools
kimi.notes: Strong on the diff-as-given. Frequent Low/nit output is skip-worthy unless convergent. China-origin provider — surface for security-sensitive repos.

kimi27.specialization: single-turn diff reasoning on Moonshot's code-specialized k2.7; rotation-pool member on the DIRECT Moonshot platform API (same billing rail as the kimi baseline, NOT OpenRouter).
kimi27.notes: BENCHED 2026-08-22 (per Gabriel): removed from select_roster.sh's draw pool, seat definition and history retained. The kimi BASELINE now runs kimi-k2.7-code itself via cli_model_alias — with file-reading tools, which this diff-only curl seat does not have — so this became pure redundancy on a provider (Moonshot) that already votes once whether one seat answers or three. Not deleted: 122 references across 17 files, 65 of them test fixtures, on the fail-closed baseline path; benching is one line, reversible, and keeps this seat's leaderboard history readable. Kimi k2.7-code via the direct Moonshot platform API (api.moonshot.ai/v1, key from MOONSHOT_API_KEY or ~/.config/moonshot/key). Added 2026-07-03 per Gabriel with draw_boost 2.5 so it would be drawn frequently while earning leaderboard data. Retired to draw_boost 1.0 on 2026-07-12 after reaching 10 sampled runs (score 72, 7/16 findings convergent) — now competes on the same footing as the rest of the pool. Same provider as the kimi baseline: kimi+kimi27 agreement counts as ONE provider vote at synthesis. China-origin provider (Moonshot) — surface for security-sensitive repos.

kimi3.specialization: single-turn diff reasoning on Moonshot's flagship Kimi K3 (2.8T MoE, 16/896 experts active, 1M context); rotation-pool member on the DIRECT Moonshot platform API (same billing rail as the kimi baseline and kimi27, NOT OpenRouter).
kimi3.notes: Kimi K3 via the direct Moonshot platform API (api.moonshot.ai/v1, model id `kimi-k3`, key from MOONSHOT_API_KEY or ~/.config/moonshot/key). Added 2026-07-18 per Gabriel, two days after Moonshot's 2026-07-16 K3 release — draw_boost was 2.5 while it earned leaderboard data; RETIRED to 1.0 on 2026-08-22 per Gabriel (enough samples), matching the kimi27 precedent. This seat is now drawn at the ordinary unboosted weight. Full open weights weren't out yet at add-time (expected 2026-07-27) — this seat hits the hosted API, not local weights. Same provider as kimi/kimi27: kimi+kimi27+kimi3 agreement counts as ONE provider vote at synthesis. China-origin provider (Moonshot) — surface for security-sensitive repos.

glm.specialization: single-turn diff reasoning; independent provider vote (Zhipu). Rotation-pool member.
glm.notes: GLM 5.3 via the OpenRouter chat-completions API — no CLI, no agentic tools; the diff is inlined (8000-line cap, same as kimi). Requires an OpenRouter key ($OPENROUTER_API_KEY or ~/.config/openrouter/key); without one the wrapper skips it. Added 2026-07-01; verified live (caught a planted one-line bug as Critical on its first run). Priors start conservative (mirroring kimi); let leaderboard.sh data drive tuning. China-origin provider (Zhipu), routed through OpenRouter (US) — surface both for security-sensitive repos. MODEL BUMPED 2026-08-22: glm-5.2 → glm-5.3 (released 2026-08-18, billed for complex software engineering and long-horizon agent tasks). NOTE THE PRICE: $0.97/M in, $3.04/M out → $1.40/M in, $4.40/M out, a ~45% rise. select_roster.sh divides draw weight by observed avg cost, so the seat self-throttles if 5.3 does not earn the difference. No draw_boost — point release, same family. MEASURED 2026-08-22 (PR #64): 5.3 is ~10x slower and much pricier per round than 5.2 — 342s and 24,170 completion tokens (23,318 reasoning) for $0.159, against 5.2's steady 32-36s. One dispatch that round hit the old 600s ceiling and died having received only whitespace keepalives, so timeout_s is raised 600 → 900. 5.3 is NOT broken: it was the only reviewer to produce findings that round (4, all verified real). It is simply a slow, expensive seat now, and select_roster.sh's cost divisor will throttle it on observed spend.

Reset expectations: treat pre-2026-08-14 deepseek leaderboard rows as a different model — and because the seat name is the leaderboard key, that reset is not automatic: draw_boost 2.5 was added 2026-08-14 so the score-52 Flash history stops suppressing the new model's chance to earn its own. Added 2026-08-22, rookie — priors conservative until leaderboard data accumulates. Cost is in line with spark and below grok; the fugu precedent (cut 2026-07-02 at $5/$30) is the bar this clears. A `thinkingmachines/inkling:free` route also exists — NOT used here: it caps context at 262k against the paid route's 1M, and free OpenRouter routes carry different data-retention terms, which matters because this skill ships private diffs. BILLING CAVEAT, measured live 2026-08-22 on a trivial 20-token prompt: 24 of 32 completion tokens were REASONING tokens, billed as output. Sticker output price is $4.05/M but effective cost per useful token is several times that, and (as first observed) a hand-set max_tokens too low returns finish_reason=length with content:null and no findings at all — the seat looks broken when it is merely truncated mid-reasoning. NOT a truncation risk as wired, though: run_reviewers.sh sends NO max_tokens on the OpenRouter lane, so the seat uses the provider default — the null-content mode only reproduces if a caller caps it by hand. FIRST ROUND (PR #64, 2026-08-22): clean, real work (6,896 reasoning of 7,486 completion on a 39k prompt, $0.066), no findings — a genuine vote. This is the shape of the fugu problem (hidden orchestration tokens billed as output) at a survivable magnitude; watch avg cost per finding on the leaderboard and cut it if it drifts toward fugu territory. draw_boost 2.5 while it earns leaderboard data; retire after ~10 sampled runs. US-origin provider (Thinking Machines Lab), routed through OpenRouter (US).

_synthesis_rules.skip_unless_convergent: Drop a single-reviewer finding at this severity unless another reviewer flagged the same file/area.
_synthesis_rules.trust_if_convergent: Promote/keep when 2+ reviewers agree; downgrade or verify when solo.
_synthesis_rules.verify: Solo finding is worth a manual look but not auto-applied.
_synthesis_rules.high_precision: Solo finding still ranks; treat as near-certain real.
_synthesis_rules.medium_precision: Solo finding ranks but apply judgment; convergence boosts confidence.
_synthesis_rules.synthesis_weight_use: Tie-breaker when reviewers disagree on severity. Higher weight wins. Also used by analyze_runlog.sh to compute weighted reliability scores.
_synthesis_rules.provider_independence: antigravity and gemini-pro share the Google/Gemini provider — count their agreement as a single provider vote when judging convergence. True independent convergence means agreement ACROSS providers; each profile carries an explicit `provider` field (openai, google, moonshot, zhipu, deepseek, xiaomi, minimax, sakana, cohere, nvidia). OpenRouter is a ROUTER, not a provider: glm through OpenRouter is the Zhipu vote, nemotron is the NVIDIA vote, etc. With a rotating roster, 3+ distinct-provider agreement is the near-certain tier.
_synthesis_rules.context_access: Second independence axis (issue #70). Provider identity is one shared blind spot; INPUT TRUNCATION is another — two seats that only saw the diff hunk can agree on a claim that needs whole-file knowledge, and that agreement is the same inference from the same partial input, not corroboration. score_findings.sh derives each seat's context_access from its dispatch lane (prompt_style: builtin_review→agent, custom_with_tools→workspace_read, diff_only_no_tools→diff_only) and upgrades it from <run_dir>/raw/<seat>.meta.json (file_context | snapshot, stamped by run_reviewers.sh) when --meta-dir is passed. A finding converges only when provider_votes >= 2 AND the sum of each provider's best context weight reaches convergence_min_capability. Do NOT hand-maintain a context field per seat — the lane is the source of truth, so it cannot drift from the dispatch code. Since 2026-08-27 the chat lanes may also run the wrapper-owned tool loop: context_access tool_read (file tools) / tool_check (file tools + the repo verify entrypoint), both weight 1.0 — a seat that read the surrounding code or ran the suite is a full capability vote.
_synthesis_rules.rotation: codex and kimi are fixed baselines (`baseline: true`) — always on. Everything else is drawn per-round by select_roster.sh, weighted by leaderboard.sh scores (see those scripts for the formula). OpenRouter fallback for first-party reviewers is ENABLED per-seat as of 2026-08-22 (see each seat's or_fallback), superseding the 2026-07-01 no-fallback rule: an account wall re-runs the lap over OpenRouter against the same model and records status "fallback", never "ok". Any other failure still drops the lap.

tool_policy._doc: Wrapper-owned tool loop for the chat-completions lanes (lib_tool_loop.sh) and the per-seat arm learner (tool_policy.sh). Arms: off = single shot (pre-2026-08-27), read = read_file/search/list_files executed by the wrapper, check = read + run_check (the repo's OWN verify entrypoint, never a model-chosen command). default_mode applies only to a seat with no chat-lane ledger data; after that the arm is learned per seat by UCB over reward = 0.6*r_q + 0.4*r_ok - cost_lambda*cost_usd (see tool_policy.sh header). A seat-level `tools: {mode, max_steps, read_budget_bytes}` pins that seat and stops learning for it. CROSS_REVIEW_TOOL_MODE=off|read|check overrides every seat for a round (auto = learn).
